idea.name: I Can Dig It RC
idea.one_liner: A staffed mobile trailer and planned store sell timed RC construction and rock-crawling play to families, adults, hobbyists, and private-event customers.
idea.customer: Children, parents, adults, RC hobbyists, birthday parties, and event organizers.
idea.offer: Timed play with RC construction vehicles and crawlers at fairs and festivals, private parties, and a planned retail venue; planned additions include memberships, competitions, an outdoor course, and light refreshments.
idea.revenue_model: Timed sessions, private and corporate event fees, planned memberships, fees for using the outdoor course, affiliate income, refreshments, and a hoped-for franchise model.

claims.quote: I convinced my wife that we needed to go to $5 for 5 minutes. She thought we both thought it was too expensive, but it doubled our business.

claims.claim: The private-party price was $399 for two hours for up to 10 people.
claims.quote: It's uh for 10 people for $399 for 2 hours, it doesn't it's not a bad deal.

claims.quote: the county fairs around here generally cost about 15 to 20 bucks to get in, and then that includes all of your rides.

claims.claim: The business paid between $100 and $550 for a week at a fair.
claims.quote: We paid as little as $100 for a week, and we paid as much as 550, I think was the most we paid for a week.

claims.claim: The couple handed out roughly 1,500 to 2,000 stickers, magnets, and other promotional items.
claims.quote: we handed out probably 1,500, 2,000 stickers and magnets and all different kind of, you know, cuz we we played around all summer with different things to hand out to parents and kids.

claims.claim: The first fair produced 10 sessions for the week.
claims.quote: we sold 10 sessions that whole week.

claims.claim: The host estimates the first event may have brought in about $50 in revenue.
claims.quote: your first event, you lost money and you maybe made 50 bucks in revenue, give or take.

claims.claim: The guest says profit is difficult to calculate because he and his wife run the events without counting their labor as an expense.
claims.quote: profit's hard because it's my wife and I running it, so we're not really spending any money to besides the the cost of the event.

claims.claim: On a bad day, events brought in about $200 to $300.
claims.quote: on a bad day we would do two or 300 bucks a day.

claims.claim: The best day brought in $800.
claims.quote: On our best day, we did $800.

claims.claim: A public event fee was $499.
claims.quote: That one was $499 because it was such an open public event.

claims.quote: Total about 3 hours with setup.

claims.claim: The best fair brought in about $2,600 over five days.
claims.quote: Probably 2,600 bucks in that neighborhood.

claims.claim: Some parents paid $20 for their child to play at the fair.
claims.quote: So, at that show we had a lot of parents who came up and were like, "Here's 20 bucks."

claims.claim: The business sometimes used a buy-two-get-one-free offer.
claims.quote: I can do basically buy one get or buy two get one free. And so, sometimes I'll ring people up like that.

claims.quote: So, we're going to do 15 minutes for 15 bucks and then as you scale time, it gets significantly cheaper per minute.

claims.claim: The trailer can ideally serve about 10 customers at once.
claims.quote: how many customers can you accommodate at the same time? Ideally around 10 is the max.

acquisition_channels.details: The trailer appeared at county fairs, festivals, and other public events; attendees could return at later events.
A Choice Hotels marketing contact encountered the business at a local event and invited it to a tailgate.
The guest described planned work with a veterans' organization, an affiliate relationship with Mountain Blocks, and event partnerships.
The business used social media; the city contacted it after seeing its social media activity.
The website and social media were listed as ways for people to contact the business; the guest collected customer emails for newsletter marketing.

ideas.delivery: The couple operates a trailer with sand and RC vehicles at events, sells timed sessions and parties, and uses a custom Replit-built app, monitor, and remotes to manage play. A planned fixed store will have construction and crawler zones; staff handle the counter, remotes, batteries, and customer assistance.

tools: Custom session tracking and POS app
RC excavators, loaders, crane, trucks, and crawlers
prices: $399 for 2 hours for up to 10 people
$100 to $550 per week for event space
$15 for 15 minutes at the planned store
